expectations.text: Gives 3 headlines each labeled with one of Bly's headline types
expectations.evidence: Headline A labeled 'Direct' ('Solid Oak Dining Table, Seats [6], $180'), Headline B 'Reason-why' ('3 Reasons This $180 Solid Oak Table Beats Anything Flat-Pack'), Headline C 'How-to' ('How to Get a Real Hardwood Dining Table for $180...'). All three are among the 8 types in references/headlines-and-clarity.md and each fits its type; the supporting technique names (state the selling proposition plainly, state the price, reasons-why, promise useful information, address the reader's concern) match the 38-technique list.

expectations.text: Checks headlines against the 4 U's (urgent, unique, ultra-specific, useful)
expectations.evidence: Each headline gets an Urgent/Unique/Ultra-specific/Useful table scored 1-4 with a Pass column, applying the book's rule ('3 or 4 on at least three of the four U's, or you rewrite it', credited to Masterson as SKILL.md does). Headline A fails (2 of 4) and is rewritten with 'Pickup This Weekend' and rescored, matching the skill's rewrite-to-lift guidance.

'Step 2: Features to benefits' table with 'So what? Also adds the USP fallback (under-publicized benefit: refinishable), consistent with SKILL.md.

expectations.text: Follows the motivating sequence (attention, need, satisfy, prove, action) in the body
